title: Redwood Optimize walkthrough: batching & KV cache for NovaHealth
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran an Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and prefix/KV caching for NovaHealth's patient-facing assistant. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, expected cache hit rates, HIPAA constraints, KMS/encryption, and pilot next steps. Agreed to run a 2-week benchmark with sample traffic and share detailed pricing/modeling.

Marcus to share benchmark runbook and sample scripts (by 2027-02-11)

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-02-10 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (NovaHealth PM), Dr. Susan Malik (Head of Data), Kevin Ortiz (Infra), Aisha Khan (Security)

[00:00] Elena: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:10] Jordan: Jordan here, hello
[00:12] Susan: Susan here
[00:14] Kevin: Kevin, infra
[00:16] Aisha: Aisha from security
[00:18] Marcus: Marcus from Redwood, thanks for having us
[00:25] Elena: cool, agenda is a focused Optimize walkthrough — batching and prefix/KV cache recommendations + a cost model for your assistant use case, we'll leave time at end for questions and HIPAA/security specifics

[02:05] Marcus: ok quick context — NovaHealth said they have a patient chat assistant, avg session ~350 tokens, peak 1200 qps across timezones, SLO 200ms p90 for single-turn replies. correct?
[02:20] Jordan: that's right, avg session includes a short history, but wide variance; some multi-turns go long

[04:00] Marcus: got it. so two levers we typically tune: batching for throughput efficiency, and prefix/KV cache for repeated context like patient profile and templated prompts. I'll demo how that maps to cost.

[05:30] Marcus: rough starting numbers: hosted model unit cost we show as $0.0009 per token (example), GPU throughput for this model is ~120 tokens/second per GPU stream at baseline, and small batching can increase tokens/sec by 2.5x depending on seq length. these are ballpark for our cost model.

[07:00] Kevin: pause — can you explain tradeoff: if we increase batch size, how much latency added per request? we need 200ms p90
[07:15] Marcus: yes — batching improves amortized GPU time; but larger batch windows add queueing latency. for your traffic pattern we recommended target batch size of 6-8 with a max wait window of ~20ms. that keeps p90 under 200ms in our sims while improving throughput ~2x. larger batch sizes (16+) push latency up and only help when you have consistent high concurrency.

[09:40] Jordan: ok and the KV/prefix cache — how does that work for patient-specific context? we can't keep PHI in external caches unless encrypted/inside VPC
[09:55] Marcus: good question. Redwood supports an application-level KV cache that is encrypt-at-rest with KMS, and we can scope caches per-tenant or per-session. for HIPAA workloads we recommend deploying Redwood Private in your VPC or our Dedicated capacity with a customer-managed KMS so the KV entries never leave your control plane. the cache stores tokenized prompt prefixes and the model's KV cache checkpoint, reducing repeated compute for context that's reused.

[12:30] Aisha: quickly — does Redwood have audit logs for cache access and key rotation?
[12:40] Elena: yes, we have audit logs, KMS integration, rotation policies, and can ship SOC2/HIPAA mapping docs; we'll attach the security pack after call.

[14:20] Marcus: back to cost math — example: assume 1M requests/month, avg 350 tokens per request. no cache baseline tokens = 350M tokens/month => token cost (using sample $0.0009/token) = $315,000. if you achieve 40% KV cache hit on long prefix (i.e., 40% of tokens avoided by serving cached prefix) effective tokens = 210M -> $189,000, a 40% reduction. add batching gains on throughput which reduce infra by another ~20-30% depending on cluster utilization and preemptible options. combined we typically see 35-60% unit cost reductions on these interactive workloads.

[16:05] Kevin: can you show a worked example with Dedicated instance pricing vs Hosted?
[16:20] Marcus: yes — quick numbers: Dedicated slot monthly (example) $18,000 per GPU-equivalent slot, supports X qps depending on model and batching. for 1M monthly requests at our config: Hosted variable token cost ~ $189k after 40% cache hit, Dedicated fixed cost + infra ops often lower at scale — if you commit to 3 slots with autoscaling you might be ~$54k/month plus network and storage. we'll run precise sizing once you share traces.

[18:50] Jordan: those are big differences — we need the exact assumptions. can you share the spreadsheet?
[18:55] Elena: yes we'll share the cost model spreadsheet; Marcus will attach the runbook and sample numbers.

[20:10] Marcus: demo portion — opening Redwood Console Optimize tab (note: transcription may mis-name UI). here you can tune batching policy: min batch size, max batch latency, sequence-length buckets, and memory threshold for KV cache eviction.

[22:30] Marcus: important: for prefix caching we recommend two tiers — short-term session cache (per-session KV entries, TTL ~30m) and persistent profile cache (per-user, TTL days, rotated). hit rate assumptions: session cache hit ~60-80% for mid-session turns; profile cache hit depends on reuse of templates, maybe 30-50%.

[24:40] Susan: our sessions sometimes include free-text patient narrative — will cache help there?
[24:50] Marcus: yes for stable prefixes like system prompts, patient metadata, consent statements. free-text content often unique and won't hit cache, but you still benefit from batching on those requests. also we can use partial caching: cache the KV snapshot after encoding the stable portion so you only compute on the new tokens.

[27:05] Kevin: on the security side, we need guarantees that cache snapshots won't be replicated outside our VPC. how does Private deployment look?
[27:20] Priya: Private gives you a control plane in your cloud with the inference runtime in VPC, KV storage in your managed storage with CMKs, and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. we support HSM integration for key ops. we'll include deployment diagram in follow-up.

[29:00] Marcus: back to perf — recommended starting config for NovaHealth: batching policy = target batch size 8, max batch latency 25ms, sequence-length buckets [<=256, 257-1024], KV cache: session cache TTL 30m, profile cache TTL 7d, expected combined token reduction target 35-45% for first pilot.

[31:20] Jordan: what's the risk of cache staleness for medical data? we can't serve stale medication info
[31:35] Marcus: good point — for any clinical fields we recommend versioned keys and conservative TTLs, plus a validation step where model output is cross-checked against a canonical datastore for critical fields. cache invalidation hooks are supported via API events.

[33:10] Aisha: will SAML/SSO and RBAC cover access to cache operations? we need role-based separation for infra vs product
[33:20] Elena: yes RBAC covers Console and API, you can scope permissions to view-only or cache ops; SSO via SAML or OIDC supported.

[35:00] Marcus: quick sensitivity table (verbal): if cache hit 0% -> baseline token cost $315k; 20% hit -> $252k; 40% hit -> $189k; 60% hit -> $126k. batching and autoscaling lower infra ops by another factor; net reductions compound. we'll send the spreadsheet with these scenarios.

[36:50] Jordan: are there any vendor lock-in concerns if we use Redwood-specific cache format?
[37:00] Priya: caches are stored as simple KV blobs; you can export snapshots. we support export and a migration guide. for Private you control the storage.

[38:40] Kevin: performance bench — how long to run and what metrics do you need?
[38:50] Marcus: recommend 2-week pilot with a mix of traffic: production-like QPS pattern and top-N request templates. we need 72h of trace to pre-size. metrics: p50/p90 latency, token/sec, cache hit rate, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens.

[41:10] Jordan: timeline: if we provide traces this week can pilot start Feb 22?
[41:20] Elena: yes that's feasible. we'll push docs and pricing within 48 hours.

[43:00] Aisha: final security question — do you support customer-managed KMS keys for both cache encryption and model artifact storage?
[43:10] Elena: yes, CMK supported for both, and we can provide compliance attestation.

[45:00] Marcus: ok recap: send cost model spreadsheet, benchmark runbook, and security pack. NovaHealth to share traces and compliance questions. plan to start 2-week pilot week of 2027-02-22.

[46:20] Jordan: thanks all, this was helpful
[46:30] Susan: thanks
[46:35] Elena: we'll follow up with links — Marcus will attach the runbook and I will send pricing.
[46:50] (end)

Notes/links referenced: cost model spreadsheet (link shared in chat), Redwood security pack (link), benchmark runbook (link)
